cards.explanation: The answer is that Paul had his head shaved to keep a vow he had made. Acts 18:18 says he had it done in Cenchrea for that reason. The text doesn't tell us what the vow was, so I'm not going to guess. I'll just say a man who keeps his word is a man I'd trust with my dough.

The answer is that Paul reasons with the Jews. Acts 18:19 says he went into the synagogue in Ephesus and reasoned with the Jews. He doesn't sit back and let the room run itself. He gets right in there and talks it through with them.

The answer is False. The people in Ephesus asked him to stay a while longer, and Acts 18:20 says he declined. The text doesn't give a reason, so I won't make one up. But he doesn't leave empty-handed, because he tells them he'll come back if God is willing (Acts 18:21).

The answer is if God is willing. Paul says, “I will come back to you if God is willing.” (Acts 18:21) He makes the promise and leaves the schedule in God's hands. Friends, I've learned that's a good place to leave it.
The answer is Jerusalem. Acts 18:22 says that after landing at Caesarea, Paul went up and greeted the church at Jerusalem. Then he went down to Antioch. Up to Jerusalem, then down to Antioch.

The answer is that Paul strengthens them. Acts 18:23 says he traveled from place to place through Galatia and Phrygia, strengthening all the disciples. Galatia and Phrygia are regions, so that's a whole lot of roads. All the disciples, too, friends. He doesn't skip anybody.

The answer is True. Acts 18:24 calls Apollos, a native of Alexandria, an eloquent man, well versed in the Scriptures. Eloquent means he could really speak. I can barely get through a recipe without losing my place!

The answer is John. Acts 18:25 says Apollos taught accurately about Jesus, though he knew only the baptism of John. The baptism of John is the one gap the verse names, friends. The verse still calls him instructed in the way of the Lord and fervent in spirit.

The answer is that they take him aside and explain the way of God more accurately. Acts 18:26 says that's what Priscilla and Aquila did after hearing Apollos. They pulled him aside, which is the gentle way to do it. If someone ever needs to fix my cookie recipe, I'd pick that way too.

The answer is False. Acts 18:27 says that when Apollos resolved to cross over to Achaia, the brothers encouraged him and wrote to the disciples there to welcome him. They didn't hold him back, friends. They backed him up with a letter.

The answer is from the Scriptures. Acts 18:28 says Apollos powerfully refuted the Jews in public debate, proving from the Scriptures that Jesus is the Christ. Remember, he was well versed in the Scriptures (Acts 18:24). Same strength, now with a fuller understanding of the way of God.
